newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, still rangebound.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end higher, still rangebound.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures finished higher on Monday as the dollar held on to its early gains, but dealers said trade was slow and the market was unlikely to break out of its recent range ahead of Japan's industrial output data.
The lead Nikkei 225 September contract added 140 points to close at 20,555 after touching a high of 20,630. Market turnover was a low 11,500 lots.
Dealers said the dollar's firm hold above the 117 yen level spurred buying of export-oriented shares in the underlying cash market.

But the September Nikkei was expected to face continued resistance near the higher end of its recent range as players would seek to take profit around 20,700 in the absence of fresh buying incentives, they said.
The July MSCI Taiwan index contract ended down 0.3 at 430.8 on volume of 1,090 lots.
The contract drew good institutional interest and activity centered around the July/August spread ahead of July's expiry on Wednesday, Refco Singapore Pte Ltd said in a daily commentary.
